annotation.authors_or_issuer: France and Germany (submitted to CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS)
key_provisions_or_claims: Propose a preliminary working definition of LAWS as fully autonomous lethal weapon systems, excluding remotely piloted, automated and tele-operated systems.
Propose a CCW political declaration affirming human ultimate decision-making over lethal force and full applicability of IHL.
Promote Article 36 AP I weapons reviews, sharing best practices and a guide tailored to LAWS.
Voluntary confidence-building: observer participation in demonstrations and information exchange between States.
Later develop a politically binding code of conduct and a CCW consultative committee of technical experts.
named_instruments_referenced: Geneva Conventions Additional Protocol I Article 36
annotation.summary_en: Working paper by France and Germany to the 2017 CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS. It proposes a working definition limited to fully autonomous lethal weapons, a political declaration affirming human control and IHL, voluntary transparency and confidence-building measures around Article 36 weapons reviews, a later code of conduct, and a technical expert committee.
annotation.title_clean: Examination of various dimensions of emerging technologies in the area of lethal autonomous weapons systems, in the context of the objectives and purposes of the Convention (CCW/GGE.1/2017/WP.4)
